headline: The S&P 500 fell 3.70% to 6,910.39 on Nov 20, entering a correction after a seventh straight loss, while the Nasdaq dropped 5.28% and the VIX closed at 35.89; futures were sharply higher Monday premarket, with a December Fed hike still about 96% priced.
regime: Hiking regime with a violent risk-off tape: the Fed funds target is 3.75-4.00%, a 25bp hike on Dec 9 is about 96% priced (CME FedWatch), the 10-year slipped back to 4.93%, and the VIX is 35.9, its highest close since late March.

lean.why: Dow futures +1.97%, S&P +2.76% and Nasdaq-100 +3.43% premarket after an $8T slide; analysts say one morning's bounce is not a recovery.

lean.t: Rates, AI doubts and PCE dominate
lean.why: Dec 9 hike is about 96% priced; PCE and GDP (Nov 25), Dell (Nov 24) and the FOMC are ahead, and the S&P is about 11.5% below its record.
Nasdaq is negative for 2026 (-2.7%), but a hiking Fed with 4.9% 10-year yields and an SEC probe of Nvidia keep multiples under pressure.

Intuit -12.77% on Nov 20; Zscaler +16% after hours on the CrowdStrike deal; tech sector fell 7.27%.
Financials -1.82% on Nov 20, better than the market; hike odds about 96% help margins; 2s10s spread 29bp.

Utilities fell 0.74% on Nov 20, a defensive group but not immune.

news.head: S&P 500 enters correction as Nasdaq plunges 5.28%
news.mean: The S&P 500 closed at 6,910.39 (-3.70%), its seventh straight loss, about 11.5% below the Oct 6 record; the Dow lost 1.93% to 48,147.33 and the Nasdaq 5.28% to 22,617.73 (-10.0% on the week, negative for 2026). Decliners beat advancers 376 to 123 and only staples rose.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp one-day index drops on heavy breadth can be followed by rebounds or further declines depending on the next catalyst; there is no fixed pattern.
news.today: Monday futures are sharply higher (S&P +2.76%), so the first hour may show whether sellers or buyers lead.
news.later: Investors may weigh whether the selloff is a valuation reset; about $8T has been lost since Oct 6.

news.head: Nvidia falls 14% on SEC accounting-probe report
news.srcN: Stock Titan, Nov 20; Capp Notes, Nov 20
news.mean: Nvidia closed at $125.53 (-14.01%), its worst day since Jan 2025 and about -23% on the week, after Reuters reported SEC enforcement staff are examining possible accounting issues and California's AG issued a subpoena over chips reaching China.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp one-day index drops on heavy breadth can be followed by rebounds or further declines depending on the next catalyst; there is no fixed pattern.
news.today: Nvidia was +8.7% premarket Monday; headlines on the probe could move it either way.
news.later: Long-term holders may watch whether the probe widens or stays an accounting inquiry.

news.head: Chip and AI stocks drop 9-16% in contagion
news.srcN: Capp Notes, Nov 20; Stock Titan, Nov 20
news.mean: AMD fell 13.25%, Micron 13.89%, Broadcom 12.19%, CoreWeave 12.02%, Arm 14.09%, Sandisk 16.05%, Nebius 16.11% and TSMC 9.48%, on doubts that AI infrastructure spending will pay back.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp one-day index drops on heavy breadth can be followed by rebounds or further declines depending on the next catalyst; there is no fixed pattern.
news.today: Premarket the group is rebounding (Micron +7%, AMD +5.8%).
news.later: Analysts called the move 'panic selling' and 'very oversold'; evidence of a durable bottom is thin.

news.head: Fed's Cook says policy is not restrictive enough
news.srcN: Capp Notes, Nov 20; Stock Titan, Nov 20
news.mean: Governor Cook said in Chile that policy is not restrictive enough and waiting 'risks falling behind the curve'; Paulson is open to back-to-back hikes. Kalshi put a Dec 9 25bp hike at 90%, with 9% for a hold; CME FedWatch is near 96%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp one-day index drops on heavy breadth can be followed by rebounds or further declines depending on the next catalyst; there is no fixed pattern.
news.later: Treasury Secretary Bessent warned the Fed could over-tighten (conservativedailynews, Nov 23).

news.head: Treasuries rally; 10-year drops back below 5%
news.mean: The 10-year closed near 4.93% (-11 to -12bp, its biggest drop since Oct 22), the 2-year at 4.63-4.65% (-13bp) and the 30-year at 5.31-5.33%; the 2s10s spread is 29bp.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp one-day index drops on heavy breadth can be followed by rebounds or further declines depending on the next catalyst; there is no fixed pattern.
news.today: Watch whether yields hold under 5% as stocks rebound.
news.later: If hike odds stay near 96%, mortgage rates may stay elevated.

news.head: Retail sales and claims beat; Michigan sentiment rises to 51.5
news.mean: Retail sales rose 0.2% (forecast 0.1%) and core retail 0.6% (forecast 0.4%); jobless claims were 203K (forecast 198K); industrial production fell 0.4%; Michigan final sentiment was 51.5 (prior 48.0) with 1-year inflation expectations at 3.7% (from 4.3% prelim); GDPNow for Q4 is 3.2%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp one-day index drops on heavy breadth can be followed by rebounds or further declines depending on the next catalyst; there is no fixed pattern.
news.today: The next hard data are PCE and GDP on Wednesday.
news.later: Firm spending alongside high inflation is the backdrop for a Dec 9 hike.

news.head: Gold and silver slide with stocks
news.mean: Gold fell about 2.4% to $3,537.77 (Capp Notes has -4.63% to about $3,515, a 14.5-month low) and silver about 3.8% to $41.22 as investors raised cash; the dollar index was flat near 103.9.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp one-day index drops on heavy breadth can be followed by rebounds or further declines depending on the next catalyst; there is no fixed pattern.
news.today: Gold has not acted as a haven in this selloff.
news.later: Investors may watch whether the dollar and real yields keep pressuring gold.

news.head: WTI rises on Iran headlines
news.mean: WTI rose 0.9-1.5% to about $83.70-83.98 and Brent to $92.57-92.63; the FT reported Trump is weighing renewed Iran strikes.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp one-day index drops on heavy breadth can be followed by rebounds or further declines depending on the next catalyst; there is no fixed pattern.
news.today: Oil-sensitive names may react to Iran headlines.
news.later: Higher oil adds to headline inflation pressure.

news.head: Intuit drops 12.8% after earnings and Mailchimp sale
news.srcN: Capp Notes, Nov 20; Stock Titan, Nov 20
news.mean: Intuit fell 12.77% after Q1 revenue rose 12% and it agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons (about $3.68B); Capp Notes says it cut its Credit Karma revenue outlook to $2.72-2.83B, while Stock Titan says profit forecasts were kept.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp one-day index drops on heavy breadth can be followed by rebounds or further declines depending on the next catalyst; there is no fixed pattern.
news.today: Sources differ on the main driver.
news.later: Software multiples are sensitive to AI-disruption worries.

news.head: Deal news: CrowdStrike-Zscaler, Global Payments, Bill Holdings
news.mean: Zscaler rose about 16% after hours on reports of CrowdStrike talks; CrowdStrike's Nov 23 8-K confirms an all-stock deal near $43.9B (1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share). Global Payments rose 9.95% on a report GTCR is exploring a takeover of about $50B including debt, and Bill Holdings fell 4.12% on a $63.25 per share TPG and Corpay cash buyout.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp one-day index drops on heavy breadth can be followed by rebounds or further declines depending on the next catalyst; there is no fixed pattern.
news.today: Merger-arb spreads and the CRWD share price drive ZS.
news.later: Regulatory review is the main remaining risk for the CRWD deal.

news.head: Gap jumps 11% on earnings; health insurers bounce
news.mean: Gap rose 11.44% on adjusted EPS of $0.82 vs $0.78 expected despite a lower full-year outlook; UnitedHealth rose 2.84% and Humana 2.63% on TD Cowen upgrades to Buy.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp one-day index drops on heavy breadth can be followed by rebounds or further declines depending on the next catalyst; there is no fixed pattern.
news.today: Earnings-driven gaps held up even in a down tape.
news.later: Insurers remain exposed to Medicare Advantage audit proposals.

news.head: Asia and Europe routed on AI worries
news.mean: Taiwan fell 6.23% (a record 17.5% weekly loss), the Nikkei 5.06%, Kospi 5.21%, the DAX 2.60% (-7.29% on the week) and the STOXX 600 2.00%; the ECB is about 95% priced for a 25bp hike on Dec 17.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp one-day index drops on heavy breadth can be followed by rebounds or further declines depending on the next catalyst; there is no fixed pattern.
news.today: Asian opens set the early tone.
news.later: Rising rates abroad as well as in the US are a headwind for multiples.

playbook: Homebuilders, REITs, utilities, small caps and unprofitable growth are pressured first. Banks and the dollar hold up better.
Housing, small caps, growth and gold benefit. Mortgage rates ease a few weeks later.
Gold and miners, emerging markets and big multinationals gain. Importers lose.
Airlines, cruise lines and shippers win. Energy stocks lose. Headline inflation eases.
A growth and small-cap rally is the usual response. Banks lose some margin tailwind.
Bonds rally, defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) lead. Cyclicals and banks get hit by recession worries.
